clue.text: Miss fantastic dame, prior to month with her in Paris

indicators.note: prior to places the reworked letters before what follows
fantastic suggests something wild and fanciful, so the letters of dame are reworked

parts.note: mois is French for month, the 'in Paris' covering this word too
elle is French for her (or she)

explanation.surface: A young woman is likened to a splendid lady, with a French flavour and a date in the diary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fantastic' rearranges DAME into MADE; 'in Paris' turns both month and her into French: MOIS and ELLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Mademoiselle is the French title for an unmarried young woman, the counterpart of the English title Miss.

clue.text: Echo for Kelvin in production of Mack the Knife?

indicators.note: a production rearranges material into a new staging, so these letters are reworked
Echo for Kelvin means Echo stands in place of Kelvin

parts.note: K is the symbol for kelvin, the unit of temperature
Echo is E in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A staging of the song Mack the Knife is suggested, with some odd tinkering by Echo and Kelvin.
explanation.walkthrough: In MACKTHE the K is swapped for E by 'for', giving MACETHE, which 'production of' rearranges. The question mark flags that a machete is one example of a knife.
explanation.definitionFit: A machete is a broad heavy blade used for cutting vegetation, so it is one kind of knife.

clue.text: Plan with detachment

definitions.meaning: a detachment of troops sent off from the main body

explanation.surface: Someone sketches a scheme while staying coolly aloof.
explanation.definitionFit: Draft covers both a rough outline of a scheme and a military party detailed for special duty.

clue.text: Actors' alien manner of speaking …

parts.note: mummers are actors in traditional folk plays
ET is the film alien, the Extra-Terrestrial

explanation.surface: Performers have a strange, otherworldly way of talking, and the ellipsis carries on into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: Mummerset is the fake West Country accent stage actors put on to sound rustic; the possessive 'Actors'' makes it fit actors' speech in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Mummerset is an invented stage dialect, a mock rural accent, so it is a manner of speaking.

clue.text: … the same as found in the middle of 'Plague'

indicators.note: found in the middle of means only the central letters are kept, with both ends dropped

parts.note: a plague is an epidemic

explanation.surface: Following on from the previous clue, it claims the same thing turns up in the word Plague.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle is taken from a synonym, not the printed word: EPIDEMIC loses EP and IC.
explanation.definitionFit: Idem is Latin, used in citations to mean the same author or work as before.

clue.text: Rapturous 19 — 'e's in a whirl!

indicators.note: being in a whirl means spinning about, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: 19 refers to the answer at 19 Across, TACTIC
'e's is he's with the H dropped, Cockney style, leaving ES

explanation.surface: Someone is overjoyed about a plan and in a giddy state.
explanation.walkthrough: The dropped H of 'e's gives just the letters ES, which join TACTIC (from 19) to be rearranged under 'in a whirl'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecstatic and rapturous are synonyms, both meaning filled with overwhelming delight.

clue.text: Main part of island is under lake and extremely wet in the west

indicators.note: in a down clue under places this piece below the others

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for lake on maps

indicators.note: in the west means the westernmost, leftmost letter of each word, which is its first

explanation.surface: A description of an island's geography: its main body lies beneath a lake and is very rainy on its western side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely wet' looks like an end-letters instruction, but 'in the west' means the left-hand letters of both words, E and W.
explanation.definitionFit: Lewis is the larger northern part of Lewis and Harris, the main island of the Outer Hebrides off Scotland.

clue.text: Disturbance on tip producing catalogue of tasks

indicators.note: in a down clue on places the first piece above the second

parts.note: a to-do is a fuss or disturbance
to list is to tip or lean over, as a ship does

explanation.surface: A commotion at the rubbish dump leads someone to draw up a list of chores.
explanation.definitionFit: A to-do list is a written list of jobs one needs to get done, so it catalogues tasks.

clue.text: Usually last in the bar to dine in support of refurbished pub

indicators.note: in a down clue a piece in support of another sits beneath it
a refurbished place has been done up and rearranged, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: to eat is to dine

explanation.surface: A drinker winds up dining at the counter of a newly done-up pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' means a musical measure, not a pub counter.
explanation.definitionFit: In music the upbeat is the unaccented beat before the downbeat, usually the final beat of a measure.

clue.text: About pain-free, though not pleasant

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for circa, Latin for about
harmless means causing no pain or injury

explanation.surface: Something is described as painless yet still disagreeable.
explanation.definitionFit: Charmless means lacking any appeal, so a charmless thing is unattractive and disagreeable.

clue.text: With bear on the turn, holler!

indicators.note: on the turn means turning round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: Pooh is the famous bear of A A Milne's stories

explanation.surface: As a bear spins round, someone yells.
explanation.definitionFit: A whoop is a loud cry of excitement, so to whoop is to holler or shout.

clue.text: 1 Across's starter borne by salver, reportedly?

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard, so a phrase is said aloud to give the entry

parts.note: something borne by a salver is on a tray, and on tray said aloud resembles the French word

explanation.surface: A young Frenchwoman's first course arrives carried on a silver platter.
explanation.walkthrough: 1 Across is MADEMOISELLE, so her starter is the French word for a first course.
explanation.definitionFit: In French, and in British menus, an entrée is the dish served before the main course, a starter.

clue.text: Crowning achievement of townscape — rebuilt after taking week off

indicators.note: something rebuilt is put back together in a new form, so these letters are reordered
taking with off means a letter is removed from the pool before reworking
off completes taking off, signalling a removal

explanation.surface: A city view is reconstructed once a week's work has been knocked off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rebuilt after taking week off' rearranges TOWNSCAPE minus W (TONSCAPE).
explanation.definitionFit: A capstone is the top stone of a structure, and figuratively the crowning achievement of a career.

clue.text: Worn-out disc I brought into operation

parts.note: EP is an extended-play record, a disc

indicators.note: brought into means the letter is placed inside the other word

parts.note: use means operation, as in a machine in use

explanation.surface: A tired-out record is pressed back into service.
explanation.definitionFit: Épuisé is a French word used in English to mean exhausted, tired out or worn out.

clue.text: Left harbour with stern intact?

definitions.meaning: a ship that has ... has left its dock, departed harbour
a docked tail has been cut short

explanation.surface: A ship sails out of port with its back end undamaged.
explanation.definitionFit: Undocked describes a vessel freed from its dock, and an animal whose tail has not been cut short.

clue.text: Spot the sharp end

definitions.meaning: the point of a pin is literally its sharp end

explanation.surface: An instruction to locate the most exposed or demanding position.
explanation.definitionFit: Pinpoint means to identify exactly, and read literally it names the tip of a pin.

clue.text: Barney undercuts flat for claimant

indicators.note: in a down clue a piece that undercuts another sits beneath it

parts.note: plain means flat, as in a stretch of level land
barney is British slang for a quarrel, a tiff

explanation.surface: A row breaks out over who undercut a rival on a flat price, leading to a legal claim.
explanation.walkthrough: Barney is British informal for a noisy argument.
explanation.definitionFit: A plaintiff is the party who brings a civil action in court, a claimant.

clue.text: Maybe estate gets swiftly into case

parts.note: an estate is a type of car, the British name for a station wagon
apace means swiftly

explanation.surface: Perhaps a property inheritance quickly ends up in a lawsuit.
explanation.walkthrough: An estate car is the British term for a station wagon; 'case' looks legal but is a protective shell.
explanation.definitionFit: A carapace is the hard upper shell of a turtle or crab, a protective case.

clue.text: Mostly seek out sweetbreads, mixing stuffing

indicators.note: out means the letters of what precedes are taken out of the other word
mixing stirs the remaining letters up into a new order
mostly means most of the word, so its last letter goes

explanation.surface: A cook hunts for sweetbreads while blending a filling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mostly seek' gives SEE, which 'out' removes from SWEETBREADS, and 'mixing' rearranges the rest (WTBREADS). 'stuffing' looks culinary but means mattress filling.
explanation.definitionFit: Bedstraw is a plant whose dried stems were once used to fill mattresses, a stuffing for beds.

clue.text: Jacket — flash! — on Romeo …

parts.note: a blaze is a sudden flash or burst of flame
Romeo is R in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A smart jacket worn by a showy lover, continued into the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A blazer is a type of jacket, often worn as part of a uniform or club dress.

clue.text: Hand signals one exchanged with ace making approach

indicators.note: exchanged means the two letters trade places, so the second swap completes the exchange
with pairs the letter for one with the letter for ace, the first replacing the second

parts.note: tic-tac is the system of hand signals used by bookmakers at British racecourses
I is the Roman numeral for one
A is the abbreviation for ace in cards

explanation.surface: Someone signals with their hands and swaps a card to make a play.
explanation.walkthrough: Tic-tac is the arm-waving code bookies use at British racecourses. 'exchanged with' swaps the I and the A in it.
explanation.definitionFit: A tactic is a planned method or way of tackling a problem, an approach.

clue.text: … stupid clothier I sacked for snigger

indicators.note: stupid suggests the letters are muddled up into a new order
sacked means the I is dismissed, removed from the letters

explanation.surface: A foolish tailor gets fired, provoking a laugh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sacked' removes the I from CLOTHIER, and 'stupid' rearranges what is left (CLOTHER).
explanation.definitionFit: A chortle is a gleeful chuckle, close in meaning to a snigger or suppressed laugh.

clue.text: Artless comeback of Milan 'Aida' crashes rather

indicators.note: a comeback is a return, so the letters are read in the opposite direction
of points to letters drawn from within the following words

explanation.surface: An opera performance in Milan goes disastrously wrong, with a naive review.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters NAIDACRA sit inside 'Milan 'Aida' crashes', reading backwards; 'rather' only smooths the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Arcadian describes the simple, unsophisticated pastoral life idealised in Arcadia, hence artless or innocent.

clue.text: Trains in Alaska perhaps, heading north, cease to run

indicators.note: in means one piece is placed inside the other
in a down clue heading north means reading upwards, backwards

parts.note: Baked Alaska is a dessert, so a pudding, PUD
RY is the abbreviation for railway, a system of trains

explanation.surface: Railways in the Alaskan wilderness head northwards and grind to a halt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Alaska perhaps' points to Baked Alaska, a pudding, not the US state.
explanation.definitionFit: To dry up is to stop flowing or run out, as a spring or source of supply ceases to run.

clue.text: Completely enthusiastic about gripping old-time …

indicators.note: gripping means holding the other piece inside

parts.note: to be into something is to be enthusiastic about it
O is old and T is time, both standard abbreviations

explanation.surface: Someone is wholly devoted to things from a bygone era.
explanation.definitionFit: In toto is a Latin phrase meaning as a whole, entirely or completely.

clue.text: Conclusion of ordinary and chaotic game

parts.note: O is the abbreviation for ordinary, as in O level

indicators.note: chaotic means in disorder, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: An ordinary match ends in disarray.
explanation.definitionFit: Omega is the last letter of the Greek alphabet, so it stands for the end or conclusion.

clue.text: Minor point involving Shakespeare's origin and existence

indicators.note: involving means taking the other letter inside

parts.note: ESE, east-south-east, is an intermediate or minor compass point

indicators.note: origin means the starting letter of the word

explanation.surface: A small matter concerning the Bard's birth and life.
explanation.definitionFit: Esse is Latin for to be, used in philosophy to mean being or existence.

clue.text: … coarse stuff from Dick?

parts.note: an abrasive powder for polishing is coarse stuff, and Dick of that surname was a British comedian of the 1960s and 70s known for saucy material

explanation.surface: Following on, a comedian named Dick produces vulgar material.
explanation.walkthrough: Dick Emery was a British TV comedian famous for innuendo; the same word names an abrasive.
explanation.definitionFit: Emery is a coarse abrasive rock ground into powder for polishing, and the surname of comic Dick.

clue.text: Moderate muscles on point, getting certain discomfort ultimately

parts.note: abs are abdominal muscles
a tine is a point or prong, as of a fork or antler

indicators.note: ultimately means the final letter of each of the words

explanation.surface: Someone toning their stomach muscles on tiptoe is bound to end up in some pain.
explanation.definitionFit: Abstinent means holding back from indulgence, especially drink, so it means temperate or moderate.

clue.text: The 'Fledermaus' in Battenberg, for one, is effortless

definitions.meaning: Fledermaus is German for bat, and BAT is a piece of the word Battenberg, a cake

explanation.surface: A performance of the operetta Die Fledermaus in a German town is no trouble at all.
explanation.walkthrough: Battenberg is a British chequered sponge cake wrapped in marzipan, so BAT, its opening, is literally a piece of it.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece of cake is the idiom for a task that is very easy.
